heading: INT. ROLLER RINK - AFTER HOURS - NIGHT

units.text: INT. ROLLER RINK - AFTER HOURS - NIGHT
A family reunion banner sags over the snack bar.
Folding tables, foil trays, a disco ball turning slowly without its light.
The floor shines.
NNEKA OBI, 70s, sits on a bench in a lavender tracksuit, skates unlaced, a paper plate balanced on her knee.
Across the floor, her son RAFAEL OBI-MENDES, 40s, bends over a speaker cable with a phone flashlight in his teeth.
His wife SOLEDAD, 40s, hovers behind him with a cake knife she has forgotten she is holding.
The grandchildren have gone to ground.
JUNIPER, 9, is under a table in full skates.
BASIL, 6, sits cross-legged on the rink's center circle, holding one wheel he has pulled off a skate.
Rafa. He's not going to come out because you fixed the music.
units.name: SOLEDAD

units.text: Then he stays there.
units.name: RAFAEL

units.text: He tugs the cable.
The speaker coughs, then plays three notes of a slow song.
She puts down the knife.
He drops the flashlight into his palm.
Nneka sets the plate aside and leans forward.
She says nothing.
She taps the bench beside her twice with two fingers.
Juniper crawls out first.
She skates a wobbling line over to the bench, arms wide, and drops beside her grandmother without a word.
Basil does not move.
He turns the wheel over in his hands and spins it, listening to it tick.
He didn't mean it.
units.name: JUNIPER

units.text: Who didn't?
units.name: SOLEDAD

units.text: Dad. About selling the house.
units.name: JUNIPER

units.text: Rafael looks at the ceiling.
He rubs his eyes with the heel of his hand, the way he did at nine, and lowers it.
Soledad moves to him and touches his elbow, and he lets her.
Nneka stays where she is.
Basil. Come here and show me what you broke.
units.name: NNEKA

units.text: I didn't break it. It came off.
units.name: BASIL

units.text: Then show me what came off.
units.name: NNEKA

units.text: He gets up slowly and shuffles over in his socks, holding out the wheel.
She takes it.
She turns it.
She hands it back and presses it into his small fist, closing his fingers over it.
Keep that. It's yours now.
units.name: NNEKA

units.text: Rafael crosses the floor, his steps loud on the maple.
He stops in front of his mother.
Soledad follows a pace behind, and the slow song drifts around the four of them.
Mama. We can talk about it tomorrow.
units.name: RAFAEL

units.text: Tomorrow I'll be eating your cake and not listening.
units.name: NNEKA

units.text: He laughs, once, surprised, and sits.
She hands him her plate.
